t: MCBP: A Memory-Compute Efficient LLM Inference Accelerator Leveraging Bit-Slice-enabled Sparsity and Repetitiveness
pb: LLM inference faces three simultaneous bottlenecks—GEMM computation in the prefill stage, weight loading during decoding (52.4% of short-prompt latency for LLaMA-7B), and KV cache loading for long contexts—which existing Transformer accelerators address in isolation at value granularity, missing fine-grained bit-level optimization opportunities.
me: MCBP is an algorithm-hardware co-design operating at bit-slice (BS) granularity. Three key techniques: (1) BS-Repetitiveness-enabled Computation Reduction (BRCR): decomposes a k-bit weight matrix into k BS matrices, groups m rows into a Group matrix, identifies repeated column vectors via a Content Addressable Memory (CAM) unit, computes a Merged Activation Vector (MAV) for repeated activations (H*(1-bs) additions), and reconstructs output via an Enumeration matrix (m*2^(m-1) additions), achieving up to 12.1x computation reduction vs. value-sparsity. (2) BS-Sparsity-enabled Two-State Coding (BSTC): stores weights in sign-magnitude format; high-order bit-slice matrices (bits 3-7 in INT8) exhibit >65% sparsity and are encoded with two states ({0} for zeros, {1,m-bit data} for non-zeros) at the same group granularity m as BRCR, achieving positive compression without requiring bit reordering for computation; low-order bits (1,2,8) remain uncompressed. (3) Bit-grained Progressive Prediction (BGPP): estimates attention scores MSB-to-LSB across multiple rounds; a radius-scaled filter (threshold = max(A_hat) - alpha * radius) eliminates Keys whose partial score falls below the threshold after each round, enabling early termination that reduces KV cache accesses by up to 50%. Hardware: CAM-based BRCR unit, lightweight parallel BSTC encoder/decoder, clock-gated BGPP prediction module, on-chip SRAM hierarchy (384KB token, 768KB weight, 96KB temp), and external HBM.
nv: A unified bit-slice-granularity co-design that simultaneously exploits bit-level repetitiveness (via CAM-based grouped matching), bit-level sparsity in high-order weight planes (via two-state coding), and progressive bit-by-bit KV cache filtering (BGPP) to jointly address all three LLM inference bottlenecks at a finer granularity than any prior accelerator.

t: TransFusion: End-to-End Transformer Acceleration via Graph Fusion and Pipelining

The DPipe scheduler partitions this Einsum DAG and applies latency-aware inter-layer pipelining across hardware memory hierarchies using dynamic programming to balance FFN and attention stages. TileSeek, a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)-based tiling search algorithm, explores the tile configuration space to balance buffer reuse against on-chip memory constraints at both cloud and edge scales.

t: FLStore: Efficient Federated Learning Storage for non-training workloads

t: Marconi: Prefix Caching for the Era of Hybrid LLMs
pb: Hybrid LLMs combining Attention and SSM (State Space Model / Mamba) recurrent layers cannot use standard prefix caching because SSM layers use in-place state updates that preclude rolling back to partial sequence states; only exact-match cache hits are possible, causing an explosion in cache entries with low reuse, wasting memory and compute.
me: Marconi maintains a unified radix tree storing both KV-cache blocks (for attention layers) and SSM state checkpoints (for recurrent layers) per sequence. Two key policies: (1) Admission: speculative insertion before prefill execution identifies branch points in the radix tree where SSM state checkpointing is needed; admits only entries in two reuse classes - (a) purely-input shared prefixes (system prompts, shared context) and (b) input+output prefixes (multi-turn conversation history). Entries not in these classes are rejected at admission time. (2) FLOP-aware eviction: utility score S(n) = recency(n) + alpha * flop_efficiency(n), where flop_efficiency(n) = FLOPs_saved_by_hit / bytes_of_cache_entry; alpha is tuned via grid search on a bootstrap period. Only leaf nodes and single-child intermediate nodes are eligible for eviction (evicting a branching node would invalidate its subtree). This prevents eviction cascades while prioritizing high-FLOP-return entries.
nv: First prefix caching system for hybrid Attention+SSM LLMs; FLOP-aware eviction metric (FLOPs saved per cache byte) that jointly considers compute savings and memory cost of cached states; speculative admission before prefill that identifies SSM checkpointing points without executing the model.

t: ProtoRAIL: A Risk-cognizant Imitation Agent for Adaptive vCPU Oversubscription In the Cloud
pb: Cloud vCPU oversubscription policies must jointly minimize overloading risk (hot nodes) and maximize utilization (stranded resource recovery), but demand patterns vary dynamically across VM types and time, making static heuristic policies either too conservative (waste capacity) or too aggressive (cause overload).
me: ProtoRAIL has three components: (1) Prototypical Imitation Learning - a trajectory encoder (LSTM or Transformer) maps CPU usage trajectories to embeddings; K prototype embeddings represent equivalence classes of usage patterns; policy is a linear layer over similarities to prototypes. Loss has four terms: Lrep (representativeness: L2 distance to nearest prototype), Ldiv (diversity: repel close prototypes), Lint (interpretability: anchor each prototype to a real trajectory), and LIMloss (imitation learning via behavior cloning or adversarial IL). (2) Active Knowledge-in-the-Loop (KITL) - identifies uncertain prototypes (high cluster entropy) and risky predictions (predicted oversubscription rate below actual usage) via a query framework; solicits feedback from domain experts (or LLMs) as up/down votes on prototypes and actions, plus merge/split operations on prototype clusters; feedback is applied via advice potential gates (exponential scaling of loss components) to steer training without explicit prior design. (3) Query scheduling - minimizes feedback budget by only querying at uncertain or risky stages.
nv: Prototypical imitation learning for sequential decision-making with explicit interpretable pattern classes; active knowledge-in-the-loop with prototype-level feedback (merge/split/vote) to de-risk policies with minimal expert queries.

t: Rethinking Key-Value Cache Compression Techniques for Large Language Model Serving

Additionally provides three tools: throughput predictor (attention-layer profiling + Vidur runtime), length predictor (BERT-based classifier predicting response length given compression algorithm), and negative sample benchmark dataset.

t: DiffServe: Efficiently Serving Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Query-Aware Model Scaling
pb: Text-to-image diffusion model serving faces two simultaneous challenges: high-quality models (e.g., SDv1.5 at 50 steps) are 4.6-18x slower than lightweight variants (SD-Turbo, SDXS), limiting throughput; and query demand fluctuates, causing static resource provisioning to either waste capacity during off-peak or fail SLOs during peak.
me: DiffServe uses query-aware model cascades with two technical innovations: (1) Discriminator design - EfficientNet-V2 trained on binary real/fake classification (real = MSCOCO ground truth images, fake = generated images from both light and heavy models). At inference, confidence score (softmax output for 'real' class) determines if lightweight model output is accepted or deferred to heavyweight model. Counterintuitive finding: using heavyweight model outputs as 'real' training labels hurts performance; ground-truth images as 'real' labels produce the best discriminator. (2) Resource allocation via MILP - Controller periodically solves a Mixed Integer Linear Program maximizing confidence threshold (proxy for quality) subject to latency constraints (execution time + Little's Law queuing delay) and throughput constraints (device counts x per-device throughput >= demand). Variables: x1, x2 (device counts for light/heavy models), b1, b2 (batch sizes), t (confidence threshold). Demand estimated via exponentially weighted moving average with 5% over-provisioning factor. MILP solved asynchronously (~10ms overhead) off critical path.
nv: EfficientNet-V2 discriminator repurposed from real/fake classification to route diffusion model queries; MILP formulation co-optimizing confidence threshold, batch sizes, and device allocation for cascaded diffusion serving under dynamic demand.

t: FlexAttention: A Programming Model for Generating Optimized Attention Kernels
pb: Every attention variant (causal, sliding window, document masking, ALiBi, paged, etc.) requires a bespoke hand-written CUDA/Triton kernel, creating an O(variants x hardware) maintenance burden and blocking rapid research iteration.

A BlockMask data structure precomputes block-level sparsity from mask_mod, enabling block-sparse FlashAttention. torch.compile lowers score_mod and mask_mod into a Triton kernel template, fusing them into a single tiled GEMM+softmax+GEMM pass. Tile-level masking avoids computing fully-masked blocks.

t: XGrammar: Flexible and Efficient Structured Generation Engine for Large Language Models

CPU-GPU overlap hides remaining mask computation behind GPU attention.

t: SOLA: Optimizing SLO Attainment for Large Language Model Serving with State-Aware Scheduling
pb: Existing LLM serving systems apply coarse-grained, fixed scheduling policies (prefill-prioritized or decode-prioritized) that cause significant latency distribution bias between TTFT and TPOT and high inter-request variance, resulting in poor SLO attainment.

A State Monitor tracks per-request TTFT/TPOT, output length distribution, and system memory usage. A Strategy Generator solves one of two constrained optimization problems at each iteration: (1) minimize max TPOT subject to TTFT SLO, or (2) minimize max TTFT subject to TPOT SLO. Hierarchical prioritization (phase-level then request-level) implements the derived strategy. A polynomial cost model (Cp for prefill, Cd for decode) predicts latency and is tuned online via a scaling ratio. Implemented on vLLM v0.4.2.

t: ThunderServe: High-performance and Cost-efficient LLM Serving in Cloud Environments
pb: LLM serving on heterogeneous cloud GPU clusters with diverse GPU types and limited/heterogeneous network bandwidth (PCIe/Ethernet rather than NVLink/InfiniBand) suffers poor throughput and high latency.
me: Two-level hierarchical scheduling: (1) Upper-level tabu search partitions GPU pool into model-serving groups, designating each group as prefill-phase or decode-phase. (2) Lower-level deduces optimal tensor/pipeline parallelism per group and orchestrates request routing via a two-stage transportation problem solved as linear programming. t: TurboAttention: Efficient Attention Approximation for High Throughput LLMs

t: ScaleFusion: Scalable Inference of Spatial-Temporal Diffusion Transformers for High-Resolution Long Video Generation

me: GPREEMPT introduces a general preemption scheduling framework that implements efficient context switching via checkpoint-restore mechanisms and intelligent scheduling policies. The approach abstracts preemption across diverse GPU architectures and workload types to minimize overhead.
nv: A unified GPU preemption mechanism that achieves both architectural generality and operational efficiency through abstraction-based scheduling.

t: Optimus: Accelerating Large-Scale Multi-Modal LLM Training by Bubble Exploitation
pb: Training multimodal LLMs is inefficient due to substantial GPU bubbles caused by heterogeneous modality models and complex data dependencies in 3D parallelism. The scheduling of encoder and LLM computations leads to idle GPU time.
me: Optimus schedules encoder computation within LLM bubbles by searching separate parallel plans for encoder and LLM components and applying a bubble scheduling algorithm. The system decomposes encoder layer computation into kernels, analyzes bubble patterns in 3D parallelism, and optimizes sub-millisecond level scheduling while preserving data dependencies.
nv: The key insight that encoder computation can be scheduled within LLM bubbles, coupled with practical algorithms that enable this scheduling across all GPUs without breaking data dependencies in the MLLM architecture.
th: GPU bubble scheduling for multimodal LLM training

me: Weaver offloads attention computation from GPUs to alternative compute resources (CPU or auxiliary memory hierarchy), reducing GPU memory pressure and enabling concurrent serving of more models. The system schedules attention operations separately and manages data movement between execution units.

t: STORM: a Multipath QUIC Scheduler for Quick Streaming Media Transport under Unstable Mobile Networks
pb: Existing QUIC schedulers do not effectively utilize multiple paths simultaneously on mobile networks where link quality varies dynamically with packet loss and latency fluctuations. Streaming applications need intelligent packet distribution across available paths to maintain quality under network instability.
me: STORM monitors per-path metrics (latency, loss rates) and adaptively schedules packet transmission across available paths based on real-time network conditions. The scheduler learns path characteristics from acknowledgment feedback and adjusts assignments to optimize throughput while minimizing buffering delays.
nv: An adaptive scheduling algorithm that dynamically responds to mobile network instability to optimize packet distribution across multiple QUIC paths.

t: DEEPSERVE: Serverless Large Language Model Serving at Scale
pb: Serving large language models at scale in cloud environments faces critical challenges in resource allocation, serving efficiency, and cold start latencies. Traditional approaches cannot rapidly elasticity-scale while maintaining performance.
me: DEEPSERVE abstracts workloads via a request-job-task model and integrates FLOWSERVE, a microkernel-inspired serving engine with NPU-centric execution and SPMD-based parallelism. It employs novel scheduling policies for PD-disaggregated and PD-colocated instances, and applies optimizations including pre-warmed pods, DRAM pre-loading, and NPU-fork to achieve 64-instance scale-up in seconds.
nv: NPU-fork optimization combined with serverless abstraction enabling sub-second cold-start scaling for LLM serving on disaggregated Ascend NPU clusters.

mx.other: 64-instance scale-up in seconds, improved cold start latencies

th: serverless infrastructure for large-scale LLM serving

t: Obscura: Concealing Recomputation Overhead in Training of Large Language Models with Bubble-filling Pipeline Transformation
pb: Pipeline parallelism in LLM training creates idle periods (bubbles) during gradient computation stages, and gradient checkpointing requires expensive recomputation. These overheads reduce effective hardware utilization and increase training time.
me: Obscura applies a pipeline schedule transformation that positions gradient recomputation tasks to execute during the idle bubble periods that occur naturally in pipeline parallelism. By overlapping recomputation with pipeline stages rather than executing sequentially, the recomputation overhead becomes partially hidden within pipeline bubbles, reducing overall critical path length.
nv: Leveraging pipeline bubble periods as hidden execution slots for recomputation through intelligent schedule transformation.
th: Hiding recomputation overhead through pipeline bubble scheduling

t: PPipe: Efficient Video Analytics Serving on Heterogeneous GPU Clusters via Pool-Based Pipeline Parallelism

nv: Applying pipeline parallelism (traditionally for training throughput) to latency-bound inference serving by exploiting comparable per-layer execution times across heterogeneous GPU classes.

t: Torpor: GPU-Enabled Serverless Computing for Low-Latency, Resource-Efficient Inference
pb: Existing serverless platforms lack efficient GPU support, preventing them from delivering high-performance inference. Sharing a node's limited GPUs among hundreds of inference functions requires minimizing latency overhead from model swapping.

t: Mitigating Resource Usage Dependency in Sorting-based KV Stores on Hybrid Storage Devices via Operation Decoupling
pb: Sorting-based key-value stores (LSM-tree based) on hybrid storage experience tight coupling where concurrent operations—background compaction, foreground writes, and reads—compete for the same DRAM cache and I/O bandwidth, creating resource dependencies that limit throughput and predictability.
